Text: If you use Cursor for coding, Claude Code for debugging, and local agents for automation, you almost certainly have a context problem.

Every tool acts like an isolated employee.

One assistant forgets what the other just learned.

The biggest bottleneck in multi-agent workflows right now isn’t reasoning.

It’s collective amnesia, combined with zero communication between agents.

@Memmy_ai just launched a smart fix for this: a local, cross-agent memory layer.

Instead of re-pasting your context everywhere, Memmy gives your stack a shared memory hub:

→ accumulate knowledge once, then use it across Cursor, Codex, and OpenClaw
→ automatically scan and import your existing agent history, so you don’t have to start from zero
→ keep your memory local, while model usage depends on your chosen provider or BYOK setup

And it isn’t just a memory plugin.

It’s a complete personal AI runtime with both MCP and a CLI.

Memmy officially launched on Product Hunt, and the team is giving early users experiencing context fragmentation a free trial with 2M GPT tokens.

Check it out and support the team with an upvote:

→ https://t.co/uxNXi2WtwB

Best part?

It’s also open-source for devs who want to build their own agents 🔥
